Q: How can I avoid wasteful copying of keys in a B-tree based STL-like map? A:

Quoting from strict aliasing rules,

If a program attempts to access the stored value of an object through an lvalue of other than one of the following types the behavior is undefined:

  • ...

  • an aggregate or union type that includes one of the aforementioned types among its members (including, recursively, a member of a subaggregate or contained union), ...

Hence going from std::pair<Key,Value> to std::pair<const Key, Value> via intermediate cast to a union or a struct containing both types as members won't break strict aliasing rules.

Caveat: std::pair in a union is not permitted until C++11, can use a structure instead.

Caveat: assumption that the two pair types have compatible layouts may not hold true. Imagine an implementation that orders first and second differently depending on the constness of the Key type.

Q: git - changes to branch since created? A:

There are 2 options.

Option 1 (shorter)
git diff origin/master...

to save results as a .patch file, run:

git diff origin/master... > diff.patch
Option 2 (longer)

Run git rev-parse HEAD, and copy the SHA1 hash, let's call it <hash>

Finally, run:

git diff <hash> HEAD

or to save results as a .patch file, run:

git diff <hash> HEAD > diff.patch

Q: PowerBi query for JIRA tickets giving results in loop A:

You're using the REST API endpoint incorrectly. If you refer to the documentation for the Search for issues using JQL enhanced search endpoint, you'll see it does not use any such parameter called startAt for performing pagination. That parameter was associated with the previous JQL search endpoints that were deprecated almost one and half years ago, as per CHANGE-2046.

I recommend that you try a public AI again for advice on how to do pagination with the new JQL search endpoints correctly, as the topic has already been extensively documented by Atlassian in How-To articles such as this one, and has been discussed extensively on many forums, such as in the Jira section of the Atlassian Community forum, over the past year and is now considered to be 'common knowledge'.

PS. Your JQL statement is incorrect as well, as you declared:

&fields=summary,duedate,status,assignee,issuetype,project

towards the end of the JQL, and ampersands (&) cannot be used to join clauses, only the word AND can be used. Putting that ampersand there invalidated the remainder of the statement.

Q: I'm trying to use the "stringdist" to fuzzy match company names between two data frames, but it's not working very good, what can be done? A:

This is a solved issue with LLMs that understand company names semantically. We built a simple utility (that optionally does some web research from complicated cases) here, it's in Python, but I used that from R via reticulate:

library(reticulate)
use_virtualenv("~/.venvs/everyrow", required = TRUE)

py_run_string("
import asyncio
import pandas as pd
from everyrow import create_client, create_session
from everyrow.ops import deep_merge

async def match_companies(companies_to_find, big_list):
    client = create_client()  # uses EVERYROW_API_KEY env var
    async with client:
        async with create_session(client, name='Company Matching') as session:
            result = await deep_merge(
                session=session,
                left_table=pd.DataFrame(companies_to_find),
                right_table=pd.DataFrame(big_list),
                merge_on_left='company',
                merge_on_right='company',
                task='Match company names. Ignore suffixes like AS, AB, Ltd, Inc, GmbH. LUMINEX and AMMINEX are different companies.',
            )
            return result.data
")

py$companies_to_find <- list(company = c("AMMINEX"))
py$big_list <- list(company = c("AMMINEX", "AMMINEX AS", "LUMINEX", "AMINEX", "ARMINEX"))
py_run_string("result = asyncio.run(match_companies(companies_to_find, big_list))")
matches <- py$result

This gives you something like:

company matched_company research
AMMINEX AMMINEX Exact match
AMMINEX AMMINEX AS Same company, AS is suffix

Unlike stringdist, it won't match LUMINEX, AMINEX, or ARMINEX because those are different companies - even though their characters are similar.

Q: Data Comparison A:

We had the same problem, and for LLMs it's a piece of cake.

We built a simple utility here that handles all three of your example cases in plain English:

import asyncio  
import pandas as pd  
from everyrow import create_client, create_session  
from everyrow.ops import deep_merge  
  
async def match_records(incoming_df, database_df):  
    client = create_client()  # uses EVERYROW_API_KEY env var  
    async with client:  
        async with create_session(client, name="Data Matching") as session:  
            result = await deep_merge(  
                session=session,  
                left_table=incoming_df,  
                right_table=database_df,  
                merge_on_left="company_name",  
                merge_on_right="company_name",  
                task="""Match records using judgment:  
                    - Address variations: E./East, St./Street, Rd./Road are equivalent  
                    - Company suffixes: LLC, Inc, Corp, Ltd are equivalent  
                    - Name variations: Ed/Edward, Bob/Robert, Bill/William are equivalent  
                    - Use address and contact name as tiebreakers""",  
            )  
            return result.data  
  
matches = asyncio.run(match_records(incoming_df, database_df))

This gives you something like:

company_name address contact matched_company matched_address matched_contact research
Acme Inc. 123 East Main Street Edward Smith Acme, LLC 123 E. Main St. Ed Smith LLC/Inc equivalent, address abbreviations, Ed/Edward
Beta Corp 456 Oak Ave Jane Doe Beta Corporation 456 Oak Avenue Jane Doe Corp/Corporation equivalent
Gamma Ltd 789 Pine Rd No confident match found

IMHO this is arguably "a more agile solution that requires less maintenance" than Levenshtein distance or SSIS Fuzzy Lookup.
